expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales. Each scale is a sum of if-statements on jet observables, clipped at zero. Each class score adds some scales and subtracts others, and the formula's validation accuracy is 65.4%. In this setup MARS was not offered the W, Z, H or top mass values as thresholds. With 8 particles the jet mass is the mass of the 8 hardest particles only, so the mass cuts the formula does use (29.6, 53.3, 60.6, 64.6, 69.6, 76.7 and 88.2 GeV) do not sit at the boson or top masses, and most neurons are built from widths (girth, girth2, width, lam1) rather than from mass. The t score follows jet size: it subtracts the compactness scale (neuron 13, girth < 0.148, -47%) and adds the overall-size scale (neuron 10, +26%), so it rises with girth, width and LHA (rank correlations 0.92). The q score is mostly the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +56%), and it subtracts overall size (neuron 10, -18%). The g score is led by a scale that falls with jet mass and subjet-pair mass (neuron 2, +38%), adds the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +22%), and subtracts the scale for pT held in the 3 hardest particles (neuron 5, -14.5%). The W score is led by the compact-centred scale (neuron 11, +24%). The Z score is led by the elongated-jet scale with mass/pT between 0.073 and 0.108 (neuron 7, +35%). Both boson scores subtract the wide-angle-radiation scales (neurons 3 and 6). W and Z are split mainly by two width-band scales: neuron 14 (width 0.0036-0.0067, mass/pT above 0.085) enters the Z score with +6% and the W score with -9%, and neuron 15 (width below 0.0132, girth above 0.102, small e2) takes -8% out of the W score and -2% out of the Z score.

Pushed down for the very narrowest jets (width < 0.00437, -7.3%; girth < 0.0761, -3.5%; lam1 < 0.00543, -2.6%) and for small mass/pT (< 0.0848, -5.2%). Overall it rises with eccentricity (rank correlation 0.555) and falls with planar flow (-0.555), N2 (-0.545) and τ21 (-0.538). Mean values: W (2.01), Z (1.93), t (0.37), g (0.16), q (0.15). It is non-zero for 76.6% of W and 78.3% of Z jets, but only 14.0% of gluon, 12.6% of quark and 19.9% of top jets.

1.title: wide jets at high total pT with small mass/pT
1.measures: Pushed down for narrow jets (girth2 < 0.00868, -10.8%, its strongest term; width < 0.0061, -7.4%; girth < 0.102, -6.3%) and when the 5 hardest particles carry more than 531 GeV (-7.9%). Pushed up by (mass/pT)² < 0.00583 (+8.0%), high total pT (log of total pT > 6.50, +6.1%, and > 6.38, +4.1%), e2_sq < 0.00817 (+4.4%) and z_7 > 0.0232 (+4.4%). It rises with girth and LHA (rank correlation 0.617) and lam1 (0.611). Mean values: t (1.31), Z (0.98), g (0.73), W (0.58), q (0.31). It is zero for 65.3% of quark jets, 51.0% of gluon jets and 13.6% of top jets.
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%) and the Z score (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: light jets: falls with jet mass and largest subjet-pair mass
2.measures: Its largest terms act on the 8th-hardest particle: z_7 > 0.0232 (-11.0%) and pT_7 < 53.4 GeV (-10.5%) push it down, while pT_7 > 20.1 GeV (+6.1%) and pT_7 < 43.5 GeV (+4.1%) push it up. It is also pushed down by LHA > 0.112 (-7.3%) and by less than 717 GeV in the 5 hardest particles (-6.5%), and pushed up by total pT < 788 GeV (+5.1%), lam1 < 0.0120 (+4.0%) and largest subjet-pair mass < 63.7 GeV (+3.7%). Overall it falls with the largest subjet-pair mass (rank correlation -0.751) and jet mass (-0.747) and rises with M2 (0.67). Mean values: g (3.57), q (2.62), W (1.70), Z (1.41), t (1.20). It is non-zero for most jets (96.3% of gluon jets, 82.0% of top jets).
2.role: It raises the g score (+38%), where it is the largest input. It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores.

3.title: wide jets with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4
3.measures: Its strongest term, girth2 > 0.00868, pushes it down (-19.4%), but girth > 0.0408 (+11.1%), width > 0.00752 (+6.8%), mass/pT > 0.0681 (+6.1%), lam1 > 0.00838 (+5.8%) and girth > 0.0761 (+4.8%) push it up, so only jets that are wide on several measures together end up above zero; τ1 > 0.0536 pushes it down (-8.2%). It follows the pT share (rank correlation 0.716) and the number of particles (0.706) at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4. Mean values: t (3.41), g (0.84), q (0.43), Z (0.11), W (0.01). It is non-zero for 75.0% of top jets but only 0.5% of W, 15.4% of Z, 18.3% of gluon and 9.1% of quark jets.
3.role: It lowers the W score (-15%) and the Z score (-22%), and raises the t score slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: small e2_sq with sizeable mass/pT (low τ21, N2, D2)
4.measures: Two terms dominate: e2_sq < 0.0117 pushes it up (+28.8%) and (mass/pT)² < 0.0117 pushes it down (-23.2%), so it is high when the jet has sizeable mass relative to its pT but a small angular spread e2_sq. Smaller terms include e2_sq < 0.0172 (+4.6%), girth2 < 0.0188 (-4.6%) and mass < 76.7 GeV (+2.7%). It falls with τ21 (rank correlation -0.618), N2 (-0.615) and D2 (-0.606). Mean values: Z (2.26), t (1.50), W (1.41), g (0.54), q (0.31). It is zero for 75.2% of quark and 63.9% of gluon jets and 17.4% of Z jets.
4.role: It raises the Z score (+4%) and the t score (+5%) and lowers the q score (-8%). It does not enter the g or W scores. Freezing it at its mean changes the accuracy by only -0.04 points.

5.title: pT held by the 3 hardest particles, small τ1 and e2

5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14.5%) and the t score (-16%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.

6.role: It raises the g score (+5%) and the q score (+9%), and lowers the W score (-9%) and the Z score (-15%). It does not enter the t score.

7.title: elongated jets (high eccentricity, low τ21) with mass/pT from 0.073 to 0.108

7.role: It raises the Z score (+35%), where it is the largest input, and the W score (+12%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

15.title: width below 0.0132 but girth above 0.102, small e2
15.measures: Pushed up by width < 0.0132 (+9.5%), width < 0.0188 with lam2 < 0.00341 (+7.4%), e2 < 0.0411 (+5.9%), τ1 < 0.0635 (+5.1%) and sj2_dr < 0.159 (+5.0%). Pushed down for e2_sq < 0.00817 (-6.3%) and < 0.0117 (-5.2%), girth2 < 0.00752 (-5.2%), girth < 0.102 (-4.8%) and girth < 0.0872 (-4.4%). So it needs a jet that is moderately wide by girth and e2_sq but below 0.0132 in width. It follows the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation 0.347). Mean values: Z (1.00), t (0.48), g (0.23), q (0.13), W (0.08). It is non-zero for 63.2% of Z jets and 12.9% of W jets. It matches the network neuron least well of the 16 (correlation 0.762).
15.role: It lowers the W score (-8%) and the Z score (-2%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

g.title: gluon: light jets with pT spread over the softer particles
g.measures: Rises with M2 (rank correlation 0.574), z_7 (0.563), z_6 (0.539) and pT entropy (0.507), and falls with the pT share of the 5 hardest particles (-0.547). It averages 2.02 for g jets, 1.09 for q and 0.92 for t, and is near zero for W (0.22) and Z (0.13). AUC 0.83 for gluons against the rest.
g.built_from: Adds the scale that falls with jet mass (neuron 2, +38%, its largest input), the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +22%), the wide high-pT scale (neuron 1, +13%) and a little of the wide-jet scale (neuron 6, +5%). Subtracts the scale for pT held in the 3 hardest particles (neuron 5, -14.5%) and the compact scale with separated subjets (neuron 0, -6%).

q.title: quark: narrow, light jets
q.measures: Falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.76), lam1 (-0.757), width, girth2 and largest subjet-pair mass (-0.756). It averages 1.92 for q jets and 1.34 for g jets, with W (0.21), t (0.04) and Z (0.00) near zero. AUC 0.86 for quarks against the rest; gluons are its main confusion (AUC 0.72 for gluons).
q.built_from: Mostly the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +56%); also adds the wide-jet scale (neuron 6, +9%) and the scale for pT held in the 3 hardest particles (neuron 5, +6%). Subtracts overall jet size (neuron 10, -18%) and the small-e2_sq, sizeable-mass/pT scale (neuron 4, -8%).

W.title: W: compact, centred, elongated jet outside the 0.0036-0.0067 width band
W.measures: No single observable follows it closely: it rises with total pT (rank correlation 0.31) and eccentricity (0.308) and falls with planar flow (-0.308) and the pT share at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.287). It averages 2.58 for W jets and 0.94 for Z jets, is slightly negative for q (-0.19) and g (-0.47), and strongly negative for t (-2.53). AUC 0.90 for W against the rest.
W.built_from: Adds the compact-centred scale (neuron 11, +24%, its largest input), the elongated-jet scale (neuron 7, +12%), the compact scale with separated subjets (neuron 0, +10%) and compactness (neuron 13, +7%). Subtracts the wide-angle scales (neuron 3, -15%; neuron 6, -9%), the two width-band scales (neuron 14, -9%; neuron 15, -8%) and a little of neurons 9 (-3%) and 8 (-2%).

Z.title: Z: elongated jet of intermediate width
Z.measures: Rises with eccentricity (rank correlation 0.47) and falls with planar flow (-0.47), τ21 with β = 2 (-0.369) and D2 (-0.358). It averages 2.38 for Z jets and 1.54 for W jets (W is its main confusion, AUC 0.74 for W), is slightly negative for q (-0.10) and g (-0.32), and strongly negative for t (-2.19). AUC 0.86 for Z against the rest.
Z.built_from: Adds the elongated-jet scale (neuron 7, +35%, its largest input), compactness (neuron 13, +7%), the 0.0036-0.0067 width band (neuron 14, +6%), the wide high-pT scale (neuron 1, +4%) and the small-e2_sq, sizeable-mass/pT scale (neuron 4, +4%). Subtracts the wide-angle scales (neuron 3, -22%; neuron 6, -15%), the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, -4%) and a little of neuron 15 (-2%).

t.title: top: wide jet
t.measures: Follows jet size closely: girth (rank correlation 0.923), width and girth2 (0.917), LHA (0.915) and lam1 (0.913). It averages 2.76 for t jets, 0.64 for Z and 0.39 for W, is near zero for g (0.07) and negative for q (-1.27). AUC 0.91 for tops against the rest.
t.built_from: Subtracts compactness (neuron 13, -47%, its largest input) and adds overall jet size (neuron 10, +26%). Also subtracts the scale for pT held in the 3 hardest particles (neuron 5, -16%) and adds the small-e2_sq, sizeable-mass/pT scale (neuron 4, +5%) and a little of the wide-angle scale (neuron 3, +2%).
